h1: Horizon City Municipal Court Ticket Lawyer — El Paso, TX
intro: Horizon City has its own police department and its own municipal court inside City Hall at 14999 Darrington Road. The court holds hearings on a set schedule, not every day, so a missed date is harder to fix on your own. For a flat $69, attorney Robert Navar appears there for you.
summaryHeading: Horizon City PD ticket? The court is at City Hall on Darrington Road
summary: Horizon City Municipal Court has jurisdiction "within the territorial limits of Horizon City for the trial of misdemeanor offenses." It sits at 14999 Darrington Road, at the corner of Darrington and Horizon Blvd, phone (915) 852-1048.

The court's posted hearing schedule is the first and third Thursday at 5:00 p.m. and the second and fourth Wednesday at 2:30 p.m.; the clerk's office is open Monday through Thursday, 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., and closed Fridays.
Citations written in Horizon City by Sheriff's deputies, DPS troopers or constables are not here; they go to the El Paso County JP precinct noted on the ticket.
Our flat fee for Horizon City Municipal Court is $69 per citation; extra tickets from the same stop are discounted add-ons. Hire online in two minutes.

sections.heading: How to Tell Your Ticket Belongs to Horizon City Municipal Court
paragraphs: Check the agency line on the citation. If it names the Horizon City Police Department and the stop was inside the city, on Darrington Rd, Eastlake Blvd, Horizon Blvd, Kenazo Ave or a subdivision street, the case is in Horizon City Municipal Court, which the town describes as having jurisdiction within its territorial limits for the trial of misdemeanor offenses. That covers the usual Class C traffic charges: speeding, stop signs, school zone speed, no insurance and registration.

The city limits are a patchwork out here. The same road can pass from Horizon City into unincorporated county or into the City of El Paso within a mile. A Sheriff's deputy, a DPS trooper or a constable who stops you on that road files in a Justice of the Peace precinct (the officer writes the precinct on the ticket), and an El Paso police officer files at El Paso Municipal Court downtown. When the agency line is unclear, use our free ticket and warrant lookup.

sections.heading: Address, Hours and Hearing Days as the Town Posts Them
paragraphs: The court is inside Horizon City Hall at 14999 Darrington Road, Horizon City, TX 79928, at the corner of Darrington Road and Horizon Boulevard. The court office phone is (915) 852-1048; the town lists the court clerk at extension 203. The clerk's office is open Monday through Thursday from 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., takes its last customer at 5:45 p.m., and is closed on city-observed holidays. City Hall is closed on Fridays and closes for lunch from 11:45 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.

Hearings are posted for the first and third Thursday of the month at 5:00 p.m. and the second and fourth Wednesday at 2:30 p.m. The town has one presiding judge and one associate judge. Citations can be paid online or by phone through the town's third-party payment vendor, which charges a service fee for card payments. Before you pay anything, remember that paying a Class C citation enters a plea and results in a conviction on your driving record.

Those hearing days are the practical reason a lawyer helps here. If you show up on a non-hearing day, or miss your date, the next setting may be weeks out, and in the meantime the court can issue a warrant. We track the schedule so you do not have to.

sections.heading: Deferral and Defensive Driving in a Small City Court
paragraphs: Horizon City Municipal Court applies the same Texas rules as every other Class C court. Deferred disposition under Code of Criminal Procedure art. 45A.302 (formerly art. 45.051) lets the judge defer the case for a period of up to 180 days on conditions, with a dismissal if you complete them. A driving safety course dismissal under art. 45A.352 is available to eligible drivers who request it on time: in general, not for speeds 25 mph or more over the limit, not for CDL holders, and not if you completed a course for a ticket in the last 12 months. Both are in the court's discretion; the town's page does not publish a local policy, and we do not assume one. Our deferred disposition and defensive driving page explains the eligibility limits in plain terms.

Horizon City has school zones on its main corridors, and school-zone speeding is one of the citations we see from the city. Courts tend to look harder at those requests, so we come to the docket ready to argue for deferral, or for a reduction to a non-moving charge when the client's record makes deferral unlikely. Insurance, registration and license tickets are presented with proof the problem was fixed, and we ask for a dismissal on that basis.

sections.heading: What $69 Covers in Horizon City
paragraphs: We charge $69 per citation in Horizon City Municipal Court. The fee covers the notice of appearance, every hearing setting, the negotiation with the city prosecutor and the paperwork to close the case. Any court fee for a deferral or course is set by the court and paid to the court. Additional citations from the same stop are discounted $10 to $30 add-ons on the online hire page. If you already have a Horizon City warrant, it is $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional one, and we handle the recall together with the ticket.

Compare that with paying. A paid ticket is a conviction, and a traffic conviction may affect insurance premiums depending on the driver's history, carrier and other rating factors. Texas no longer uses the former Driver Responsibility Program points system, but DPS may suspend the license of a "habitual violator" — four or more moving-violation convictions arising from separate incidents within 12 consecutive months, or seven or more within 24 months (Transp. Code §521.292(b)). The consultation is free. Se habla español.

sections.heading: Missed a Horizon City Hearing Date? Warrants and License Holds
paragraphs: If your appearance date passes without a plea or an attorney's appearance, the court can issue a warrant and a separate failure to appear charge can follow. In general, an unresolved case can also be reported to the state's Failure to Appear program, which blocks a DPS license renewal until the court clears the hold. Because the court hears cases on set days, a self-represented driver who shows up to fix it can wait longer than at the downtown court.

We file the appearance, ask the court to recall the warrant and have the ticket reset for the next hearing day, the same process described on the traffic warrant recall page. Warrant recall timing depends on the court's docket; many El Paso courts act within days once an attorney files, but timing cannot be promised.

faqs.q: Where is Horizon City Municipal Court?
faqs.a: Inside City Hall at 14999 Darrington Road, Horizon City, TX 79928, at the corner of Darrington Road and Horizon Boulevard. The court office phone is (915) 852-1048. The clerk's office is open Monday through Thursday, 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., and closed Fridays.

faqs.q: When does Horizon City Municipal Court hold hearings?
faqs.a: The town posts hearings for the first and third Thursday at 5:00 p.m. and the second and fourth Wednesday at 2:30 p.m. Dates can change, so confirm with the court or let our office handle the setting for you.

faqs.q: Which tickets go to Horizon City Municipal Court?
faqs.a: Misdemeanor citations written within the territorial limits of Horizon City, which in practice means Horizon City Police tickets. Sheriff, DPS and constable citations in the same area go to the El Paso County JP precinct noted on the ticket.

faqs.q: What is the attorney fee for a Horizon City ticket?
faqs.a: A flat $69 per citation. Extra tickets from the same stop are $10 to $30 add-ons, and warrant recalls are $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional one. Court fees are set by the court and paid separately.

faqs.q: Do I have to go to court in Horizon City?
faqs.a: Generally not. We file the appearance and attend the hearing for you. You would need to appear only if the case were set for trial, which we would discuss with you first.

faqs.q: I live in Horizon City but an El Paso officer wrote the ticket. Which court?
faqs.a: El Paso Municipal Court downtown, because the issuing agency decides the court, not your address. Our fee there is $59. Use the free lookup form if you are unsure.
